facts.raw_span: a 1-year history of slow but progressive swelling near her gluteal cleft
denied fevers, chills, pain, drainage, bleeding, or rectal bleeding
a 4 × 4 cm area of swelling just left of the natal cleft at the level of the tip of the coccyx
mild blanching erythema of the overlying skin but no fluctuance, purulence, or visible pilonidal pits
no fluid was obtained
a complex and septated 6 × 4 × 4 cm mass was excised from the subcutaneous tissue near the coccyx
the mass was adherent to subcutaneous fat but did not involve the coccyx or anal sphincter
a high suspicion for abscess
the differential diagnosis at this time included inclusion cyst and soft-tissue tumor
percutaneous aspiration was performed in clinic
a 6-cm vertical incision was made over the lesion in the prone jack-knife position
the specimen was oriented with sutures and sent for permanent pathology

concepts.why: The patient presented with a 1-year history of slow but progressive swelling near her gluteal cleft, and the excised mass was complex and septated, consistent with a pilonidal cyst.
The patient's differential diagnosis included inclusion cyst, and the excised mass was consistent with a benign cystic lesion.
The patient's differential diagnosis included inclusion cyst, and the excised mass was consistent with a benign cystic lesion.
The patient's differential diagnosis included soft tissue tumor, and the excised mass was complex and septated, consistent with a neoplastic process.
The excised mass was adherent to subcutaneous fat, consistent with a lipoma.
The patient had a high suspicion for abscess, and percutaneous aspiration was performed, although no fluid was obtained.
The patient presented with mild blanching erythema of the overlying skin, consistent with an infected cyst.
The patient presented with mild blanching erythema of the overlying skin, consistent with an infected cyst.

rationales.F01: The patient's 1-year history of progressive swelling near the gluteal cleft suggests a possible cyst or tumor.
rationales.F02: The absence of fevers, chills, pain, drainage, bleeding, or rectal bleeding makes an abscess or infected cyst less likely.
rationales.F06: The excised mass was complex and septated, which is more consistent with a soft tissue tumor or lipoma than a cyst.
rationales.F08: The initial suspicion for abscess was high, but the absence of fluid on aspiration and the presence of a complex mass on excision suggest otherwise.
